welcome.title: Name this machine
welcome.desc: A couple of quick basics before the array - both are already set to sensible defaults and can always be changed later from Settings → About.

start.title: Let's build your array
start.desc: Every disk that's part of the array - one or two parity disks plus your data disks - needs to be assigned before it can start. If this isn't a fresh install, you can bring an existing array's configuration in instead of assigning disks by hand.
start.buildChoiceDesc: Assign a parity disk and your data disks now. You can always add more later.
start.importChoiceDesc: From a previous NonRAID install, or another array using the same superblock format.
start.restoreChoiceDesc: Bring back everything from a previous nonraid-webui install at once - array, shares, users, and settings - from a config backup archive.

restoreConfig.title: Restore a full config backup
restoreConfig.desc: Bring back everything from a previous nonraid-webui install at once - array, shares, users, and settings. Pick where the backup is coming from.

disks.title: Build your array
disks.desc: Pick a parity disk and a data disk, then press Build Array. Initialization - clearing the data disk and building parity - happens in the background, so you don't need to wait here. Once it's running, add more disks, a second parity disk, or a cache mirror any time from the Disks page.

apps.title: Install ready-made apps
apps.body: The Apps catalog has one-click installs for common self-hosted services - media servers, downloaders, home automation, and more. Find it any time from the sidebar.

docker.title: Or run your own containers
docker.body: Bringing your own image? The Docker page pulls it, sets ports/volumes/env vars, and shows a live log tail - no app catalog entry needed.

lxc.title: Or a full lightweight VM
lxc.body: When a container isn't isolated enough, LXC gives you a more complete lightweight VM instead - with its own storage location, separate from Docker's.

notifications.title: Stay in the loop
notifications.body: Turn on notifications in Settings to hear about it - by email, Discord, or anything Apprise supports - when a disk fails, a parity check finishes, or something needs a look.

backups.title: Don't lose this setup twice
backups.body: Back up this app's own config - array, shares, users, and settings - locally or to a remote via rclone. Settings → Backups sets it up; Settings → Recovery brings it back, from an upload, a local backup, or a remote one.

done.title: You're all set
done.desc: Head to the Dashboard to check on the array, or Disks to keep adding storage. You can replay this tour any time from Settings → About.

RemoteRestoreOnboarding.rcloneNotInstalled: The rclone package isn't installed on this host - re-run tools/install-webui.sh on it to enable remote backups.
RemoteRestoreOnboarding.titleRecoverArray: Recover the array from a remote backup
RemoteRestoreOnboarding.pickRemoteDesc: Pick a remote to browse for backups already sitting on it, or connect a new one.

pathStep.descAfter: did the old install's sync job point? Leave blank to browse the remote's own root.
